correctness.rationale: For arbitrary b with distinct primes p,q and any T,N, factor T as its b-smooth part and coprime part, select k with T_parallel|b^k and b^k>=N, then by CRT construct u≡0(p),1(q),1(T_perp). Indices n=b^k,m=b^ku are congruent modulo T. The equalities n^n=b^{kn}, m^m=b^{km}u^m and q∤u imply exactly nu_b(n^n)=kn and nu_b(m^m)=km. Hence F_b(n)=1 but F_b(m)=u^m mod b is divisible by p. This treats all bases/multiplicities and all possible periods; it depends only on CRT. The prime-power classification is explicitly imported from [1, Theorem 7/Prop 10]. The extracted standalone verifier passes 352 CRT constructions, 75 direct huge-integer checks, and 512 positive-case period checks; finite checks corroborate but do not prove the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2012 initiating paper explicitly states the arbitrary-base iff as Conjecture 11 and proves only the prime-power classification and selected composite classes. The universal mixed-prime CRT obstruction is a strictly stronger new theorem than its even-squarefree subcase: it handles bases such as 12, 18, 45 and all other two-prime-support bases and every possible period. The 2023 full article addresses analytic-function valuations/automaticity, not the global variable-exponent self-power periodicity claim. Exact base-12 OEIS data are finite sequences, not an all-period theorem. Six targeted mathematical research-record searches and four own-week/archival ledgers found no implication. The positive cases are acknowledged as previously established. This is a best-knowledge scientific-priority assessment, not a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The theorem settles the explicit full-base Conjecture 11 of a 2012 number-theory paper, replacing partial examples with an infinite exact classification. The CRT construction is useful structurally because it manufactures contradictions for every proposed eventual period, at arbitrary thresholds, without any squarefree restriction. The result is not a mere recomputation of digit values or a relabeling of the known prime-power theorem; even though the obstruction proof is short, completing the natural conjecture is a motivated and substantial resolution.
